text:
ashley: Anyone else seeing intermittent DNS failures from model-fetch on newly provisioned GPU nodes in us-west-2? getting NXDOMAINs for internal service names for ~10-30s after node comes up

mike: saw a spike in 5xx from model registry yesterday, could be related. any recent change to egress/proxy?

ashley: nope, no proxy changes. pattern: node comes up (autoscaler), kubelet schedules pods, then pods doing model pull hit NXDOMAIN on svc.kube-... names. after ~20s they recover.

julian: can you paste /etc/resolv.conf from a bad node? my hunch: resolv order/resolver handoff problem between systemd-resolved and kubelet-generated resolv.conf

ashley: paste below from an affected node:
```
# /etc/resolv.conf (container)
nameserver 169.254.20.10
search svc.cluster.local cluster.local us-west-2.compute.internal
options ndots:5 timeout:2 attempts:2
```
Notably, ndots is 5, so short names are getting search-suffixed a lot.

sara: ndots:5 is default for our container runtime image? that will cause `api` -> `api.svc.cluster.local` retries and trigger extra queries. but still shouldn't produce NXDOMAIN long enough to blow model pulls.

mike: could be a negative cache/TTL issue on the edge stub resolver. If upstream returns SERVFAIL or DNS64/NAT behaviour, negative cache could propagate across pods behind the same NAT port.

infra-oncall: deploy-bot just posted a nodepool image rollout 12:45 UTC, matches timeline. deploy-bot: `deploy stack/gpu-nodeimage v2.3.1 -> v2.3.2`

aws: prod edge NAT gateway logs show bursts of ephemeral port reuse -> potential conntrack/nat exhaustion on egress layer. when that happens, clients see UDP drops and fall back to TCP which adds latency and occasionally returns SERVFAIL.

julian: that explains flakiness. UDP DNS to our upstream (169.254.20.10) sometimes drops, systemd-resolved falls back to TCP or times out. combined with ndots causing more queries = more load = more failures.

ashley: quick reproduction: on a repro node I ran `dig api.svc.cluster.local @169.254.20.10 +time=1 +tries=2` and got NXDOMAIN for ~25s then OK.

sara: workaround ideas: 1) reduce ndots to 1 in container resolv.conf templates 2) bump systemd-resolved cache positive TTL for local svc records 3) make our kubelet point to a local caching stub on node (127.0.0.53) that does UDP retry/backoff

mike: also look at ephemeral port range for pods behind kube-proxy -> if ephemeral ports are low, NAT reuse causes collisions that drop UDP. increasing ephemeral range + conntrack tuning helped before.

julian: long term: move to node-local caching agent (nodelocaldns) on GPU nodes so lookups for cluster.local never hit egress NAT. also ensure startup script doesn't clobber resolv.conf ordering (we had a bug: cloud-init wrote system resolvers before kubelet stub).

ashley: created a temporary daemonset to restart systemd-resolved on boot for new nodes; will monitor. also opened a ticket to patch node image to set ndots:1 and install node-local-dns in GPU pool.

infra-oncall: assigning to julian/mike/sara for rollout plan and mitigation timeline. please post ETA in this thread.

julian: I'll do an image patch in canary pool today (ETA 3h) to set ndots:1 + node-local-dns. mike will validate conntrack/ephemeral tuning. sara to propose TTL/caching config.

mike: I'll validate NAT metrics and ramp conntrack settings in staging. if stable we can apply to prod pools tomorrow.

ashley: thanks — leaving monitoring alerts on: dns.nx_rate, nodepool:cold-start-errors. ping here when canary finishes. :thumbsup:
